ai.title: Fix reading edited files in main-prompt
ai.summary: Updated `getFileReadingUpdates` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to filter messages by `assistant` role before parsing file blocks. This prevents user messages containing `<write_file` strings from being incorrectly identified as edited files. Scope limited to backend main prompt logic. Follow-up constraint: ensure user prompts do not trigger file update logic.

eli5.text: Only assistant messages are now treated as file-editing activity when reading edited files in the main prompt logic. This prevents user messages containing '<write_file' strings from being mistakenly parsed as edited files. The change affects backend prompt processing and is live today. If you looked, you'd notice user prompts no longer accidentally trigger file update logic in the backend main prompt system.

eli5.text: The AI assistant software got a routine internal version bump to keep installations up to date. The actual user-facing improvements are bundled inside this version, but this specific change is just the version number being ticked up by one.

ai.title: Gemini fallbacks use internal keys and OpenRouter
ai.summary: Gemini 2.5 Pro streaming fallbacks now prioritize internal API keys and OpenRouter endpoints, removing user-key and Vertex AI attempts. This simplifies the retry chain to Internal Gemini, OpenRouter Free, OpenRouter Preview, then Claude Sonnet. The change affects backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts and adds openrouterModels to common/src/constants.ts. Cost tracking for openrouter_gemini2_5_pro_preview was added to message-cost-tracker.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to use Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro model to generate a response, and that first attempt fails, it now automatically tries a different set of backup routes to get the job done. These backup routes use the assistant's own credentials and a service called OpenRouter instead of your personal Google account keys or Google's enterprise platform. The result is that if you're chatting with the assistant and it's working hard on a complex task using Gemini, you're less likely to hit a wall if something goes wrong on Google's end. This behavior is already active.

ai.summary: Deleted `displayGeminiKeyPromptIfNeeded` and associated state from `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Removed logic that prompted users for a Gemini API key when in max mode. This eliminates a temporary workaround implemented while waiting for Gemini 2.5 Pro availability.

eli5.text: The CLI no longer asks you for a Gemini API key when you use max mode, because the assistant now handles Gemini access internally using its own keys and OpenRouter. If you use the command-line tool in max mode and don't already have a Gemini key stored, you will no longer see a yellow pop-up telling you how to create one. The only group this touches is you, anyone running the tool in max mode who wasn't already authenticated with a Gemini key, and it is live today.

ai.title: Add Gemini API preview step to stream fallback chain
ai.summary: Inserts Gemini API direct call for `gemini-2.5-pro-preview` as step 3 in `streamGemini25ProWithFallbacks`, shifting OpenRouter preview to step 4. This prioritizes internal Gemini key usage over OpenRouter for preview models before final Claude Sonnet fallback. Scope limited to `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts`. Log message updated to reflect new fallback target.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to answer you with a newer Gemini model and the first option fails, it now tries a second Gemini endpoint directly before falling back to a third-party routing service, then finally to the Claude model. This means that in the middle of your request, instead of going through an external provider for the preview version of the model, it will use an internal key to call Gemini directly. You wouldn't see this switch yourself, but it could make the assistant slightly faster or more reliable when it needs to use that preview model.

ai.title: Constrain tool usage to listed tools in main prompt
ai.summary: Added explicit instruction to backend/src/main-prompt.ts to restrict tool usage to the `TOOL_LIST`. This prevents unintended display issues when the model hallucinates unlisted tools. Scope limited to the backend prompt generation logic.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant, it can now only run the specific tools we've told it about, rather than making up tools that don't exist. This should prevent confusing messages or blank responses caused by the assistant trying to call tools that aren't actually available. The change is live today for all internal requests that use the main system instructions. If you were to test it, you would not see the assistant attempting to use unfamiliar tools or producing the display glitches that sometimes accompanied them.
